data.narrative:
Telexistence is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jin Tomioka and Ken Tomoyose that has raised $170M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, and Exotec.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement to the $170M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $323M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), yielding a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B–$2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range of $275M to $2.0B, with a median of $1.0B. The substantial gap between stage-progression ($323M) and peer-median ($1.8B) reflects material uncertainty around whether Telexistence trades at a discount or premium to peer valuations. Key variables include the specificity of peer-stage alignment, timing of recent peer valuations, and the company's relative position on capital efficiency and product maturity within the robotics cohort. Resolution of these factors is essential to narrowing the valuation band.
